subject: Decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment / SLA — follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Reddy <priya.reddy@finova.com>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@finova.com>

Subject: Follow-up & quick clarifications from today’s call

Hi Tom / team —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying questions so we align on next steps: 

1) Decision criteria we heard today (please correct me if I missed anything):
   - Latency target: 95th percentile under 200ms for conversational endpoints (customer-facing chat).
   - Cost sensitivity: focused on $/1k responses metric; internal target to reduce current token spend by ~30%.
   - Deployment preference: must support private deployment (VPC) with on-prem option for regulated workloads; open to hybrid for pilot.
   - SLA: enterprise SLA required (99.9% uptime) plus clear incident notification and audit logs.

2) Stakeholder map — please confirm the primary economic buyer and procurement/security contacts:
   - Economic buyer: Maria Lopez (CFO) — confirmed on the call?
   - Procurement: Ian Baxter — will handle T&Cs/redlines.
   - Security: Priya Reddy — reviewing SOC2, data residency, and KMS requirements.

3) Open items we promised to follow up on:
   - Concrete latency benchmarks across model sizes and expected load.
   - Deployment options doc + preliminary pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
   - Draft SLA language and evidence for auditability (log retention, access controls).

I’ll loop in Neha (SE) to provide the latency/cost tradeoff table and suggested configuration for an initial pilot. After that, we can propose a short MAP and draft MSA redline milestone.

Would love any clarification on the latency target (200ms p95) — is that for peak traffic or for the steady-state pilot? Also, is the 30% cost reduction target versus any specific current baseline?

Next steps: we’ll send a short technical note + pilot config by EOD Friday. Can you confirm your preferred meeting time for a procurement/security alignment next week?

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Follow-up & quick clarifications from today’s call

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. A few answers/clarifications: 

- Latency: the 200ms p95 is our goal for the live pilot (customer-facing). For internal bulk processing (async jobs) higher latency is acceptable, but pilot needs to meet the p95 target under expected burst load (we estimate ~150 concurrent conversations at peak).

- Cost baseline: Maria, for context, we run roughly $45k/month today on our current provider for chat features. The 30% reduction is a target to present to finance; we can be flexible based on SLA and data controls.

- Deployment: we prefer Private (VPC) for the pilot if it’s not prohibitive. If Dedicated with private networking is significantly cheaper and meets data residency/KMS needs, that could be a good compromise.

- SLA: 99.9% is the bar for production; for pilot, we can accept a lower tier if there are clear upgrade paths and an SLO-based rollback plan.

We’re available for the procurement/security sync Tue/Wed next week (any time after 11am PT works).

One more ask: can you send a short appendix that maps SLA items (uptime, incident response, data retention, breach notification) to contractual language so Ian has a head start on redlines?

Thanks — looking forward to Neha’s note.

Best,
Tom
Head of Product — Finova

Subject: Re: Decision criteria: latency / cost / deployment / SLA — follow-up

Hi team —

Attached a short note (redwood-deployment-options.pdf) and a latency / cost appendix. Quick summary here: 

Pilot recommendation (targeting Tom’s 200ms p95 at ~150 concurrent):
- Option A (Private - VPC on Dedicated GPUs): best latency predictability; p95 ~120–180ms depending on model size. Cost: estimated $31k–$37k/mo for pilot scale (includes reserved capacity + private networking).
- Option B (Dedicated w/private networking): slightly lower cost (~$25k–$30k/mo) but p95 can vary 160–220ms depending on burst characteristics; can be tuned with burst capacity.
- Option C (Hosted + strict routing to region + customer-managed VPC peering): cheapest to start but requires trust on data plane; p95 generally 170–260ms.

Notes on SLA / contractual language request: I attached a one-page mapping called Finova_SLA_Request_v1.pdf that lays out how our standard SLA maps to the items you listed (uptime, incident response windows, audit logs, retention). For pilot we can offer an accelerated path to 99.9% SLA once we complete the pilot validation and commit to dedicated capacity.

Next steps we propose:
- Technical pilot: 4 weeks, Dedicated Private pool, smoke test with 10% of traffic ramping to full peak over 7 days.
- Deliverables: Latency benchmarking report, token-cost summary, and configuration checklist for KMS and SSO.

I’ve attached the files and included estimated monthly ranges; we can firm numbers after we lock model selection and expected QPS.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf; Finova_SLA_Request_v1.pdf

Marissa / Neha —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and attachments — skimmed the SLA mapping and deployment note. A few procurement items before we progress to legal redlines: 

1) Can you confirm incident response RTO/RPO expectations and cosmetic wording for breach notification (we prefer 72 hours initial notification + 30-day remediation plan).
2) Do you support SOC 2 Type II evidence sharing under NDA? If yes, please indicate the process and timeline.
3) For pilot pricing, would you be able to provide a one-month trial credit or reduced rate to validate latency/cost? We typically require this to move to an MSA discussion.

If you can send a short doc with bullet answers to the three questions, I’ll circulate to legal and security next week. Also proposing Tue 21 Jul 11:30am PT for the procurement/security sync — ok for your side?

— Ian
